post.text:
🚨 BREAKING: Google Research just dropped the textbook killer.

Its called "Learn Your Way" and it uses LearnLM to transform any PDF into 5 personalized learning formats. Students using it scored 78% vs 67% on retention tests.

The education revolution is here. https://t.co/O8ka4IfvPS

The problem with textbooks? They're one-size-fits-all nightmares.

Google's solution is brilliant: AI reads your interests (sports, music, food) and your grade level, then rewrites every example to match what you actually care about.

Physics becomes relatable. History becomes personal.

But it doesn't stop at personalization.

The system generates 5 completely different ways to learn the same content:

- Interactive text with embedded questions
- Audio lessons with AI teacher conversations
- Narrated slides with fill-in-the-blanks
- Mind maps you can zoom in/out
- Section quizzes

The tech stack is insane.

LearnLM (built into Gemini 2.5 Pro) handles personalization. Multi-agent pipelines generate representations. They even fine-tuned a dedicated model just for educational illustrations.

State-of-the-art models couldn't handle educational visuals properly.

Google tested this with 60 Chicago students, ages 15-18. Randomized controlled trial. 40 minutes to learn about brain development.

Results were brutal:

Learn Your Way: 78% retention after 3-5 days
Traditional PDF: 67% retention
100% felt more comfortable vs 70% with PDFs https://t.co/MBTXGa4rfw

Three education experts rated the AI content 0.85+ on every metric.

Accuracy, coverage, learning science principles - everything passed.

This isn't a demo. It's production-ready AI that actually improves learning outcomes.

93% of students want to use it for future learning. https://t.co/47etakPMaG

You can try it right now on Google Labs: https://t.co/vdI7CcI3e8

Lessons on immune systems, economics, sociology. Each adapts to your grade and interests in real-time.

We just watched Google delete the entire textbook industry.

Static learning is dead. Personalized AI education is here.

Looking for more posts like this?

Follow me @thisguyknowsai and you'll get 1x post every single day.

And don't forget to repost the thread to reach more.

Thanks for checking! https://t.co/hnqLx7MtcB

comments.name: Consciousnes
comments.text:
Here is an in-depth study of the system:

Both documents defend a common thesis: we still evaluate complex systems : artificial intelligence, economics, cognition based on their visible performance, confusing functional appearance with structural reality.

Whether it concerns the opposition between generative AI and agentic AI, or the surface indicators used to measure intelligence, value, or stability, the observation is the same: these distinctions mask shared internal limitations and a profound fragility. A system can produce impressive results while remaining structurally unstable.

The central issue, therefore, is not what the system does, but what constrains it, stabilizes it, and prevents it from drifting. The CBD (Constraints – Equilibrium – Dynamics) framework thus proposes a unifying principle: only a cumulative internal dynamic, based on persistent constraints and endogenous regulation, makes a system reliable, controllable, and sustainable.

https://t.co/UKZVO0WMcr

comments.name: Andras Dobos
comments.text:
This is not just about being a textbook killer. It’s about the end of education’s social contract. For centuries, that contract was based on scarcity and utility. You learned a skill to become needed and being needed gave you a place in the world.

AI demolishes that as it makes expertise abundant and cheap. When knowledge is instant and personalized, what is the economic value of the person who spent years acquiring it? The tool isn’t the revolution. The crisis of purpose it triggers is.

comments.text:
The LearnLM piece is wild but here's what's got me thinking: the 60 student sample from Chicago, right. But what does adoption look like for a teacher who's already drowning in other tools? Personalization tech wins when the friction of setup is lower than friction of not using it.

The real test isn't retention scores. It's whether schools actually deploy this or if it becomes another sandbox demo. Tech graveyard is full of better solutions that lost to simpler adoption curves.
